about_page.title: About Studio344
about_page.tagline: A personal hobby account for someone who loves technology and building things.
about_page.mission_desc:
Studio344 is a personal hobby account for someone who loves technology and building things.
It's a space where I freely experiment with interesting tech and enjoy personal development, separate from work.

If something looks fun, I just start building it.
With that mindset, I casually create web apps, tools, and whatever else catches my interest.
about_page.profile_desc:
Working as an engineer at a global IT company.

In my free time, I tinker with technologies that catch my eye (React, Next.js, WebGL, etc.)
and build small tools to solve everyday inconveniences.
about_page.philosophy_desc:
Rather than aiming for perfection, I prefer to just make something that works first.
Because it's a hobby, I can challenge new things without worrying about failure.

portfolio_page.title: Portfolio
portfolio_page.subtitle: An immersive portfolio site featuring Bento Grid design
portfolio_page.feature1_desc: Built with pure JavaScript and CSS only, without React or Vue. Achieved near-perfect Lighthouse scores with ultra-fast load times.
portfolio_page.feature2_desc: Linking CSS variables with JS to create a spotlight effect that follows mouse movement and noise textures via SVG filters.
portfolio_page.feature3_desc: Smooth Japanese/English language switching powered by the i18next library. Designed with global content delivery in mind.
portfolio_page.design_desc: Designed with the concept of being modern and futuristic while maintaining information readability. Adopting the trending Bento Grid layout to balance accessibility and visual beauty.
portfolio_page.tech_intro: Built on web standards without framework dependencies. Lightweight yet capable of rich visual expression.
portfolio_page.tech_html: HTML5 / CSS3: Semantic markup with CSS variables, Grid, and Flexbox for responsive layouts.
portfolio_page.tech_js: Vanilla JavaScript: All features built with plain JS. Zero bundle size overhead.
portfolio_page.tech_gsap: GSAP + ScrollTrigger: Scroll-driven animations and smooth transitions.
portfolio_page.tech_i18n: i18next: Bilingual (JA/EN) support with dynamic language switching — no page reload needed.
portfolio_page.tech_hosting: GitHub Pages: Zero-cost static hosting with custom domain + HTTPS.
portfolio_page.perf_desc: Thanks to the framework-free approach, the site achieves high Lighthouse scores. External dependencies are kept minimal for fast initial loads.
portfolio_page.perf_score: Lighthouse Score: 95+ (Performance / Accessibility / Best Practices / SEO)
portfolio_page.perf_deps: External Deps: GSAP + i18next only (no bundler configuration)

ucfitness_page.title: UCFitness
ucfitness_page.subtitle: A group fitness tracking platform powered by the Fitbit API
ucfitness_page.features_intro: UCFitness serves as the ultimate social fitness dashboard, offering three core features.
ucfitness_page.feature1_desc: Track rankings in real time. Compare steps and activity levels with colleagues and friends on a daily, weekly, and monthly basis.
ucfitness_page.feature2_desc: Join a group and compete in team battles. Compete not just on individual scores, but on the combined totals of your entire team.
ucfitness_page.feature3_desc: Unlock unique badges by reaching milestones or maintaining streaks. Visualize your achievements.
ucfitness_page.tech_intro: Built with a modern web technology stack for a fast and scalable application.
ucfitness_page.tech_frontend: Frontend Framework: Next.js (App Router) - Fast initial rendering with server components.
ucfitness_page.tech_ui: UI Library: TailwindCSS & Shadcn/UI - A beautiful and consistent design system.
ucfitness_page.tech_auth: Authentication: OAuth 2.0 (Fitbit Web API) - Secure token management with automatic refresh.
ucfitness_page.tech_db: Database & Realtime: Supabase (PostgreSQL) - Used for real-time leaderboard updates (Live Subscription).
ucfitness_page.tech_deploy: Deployment: Vercel + Cloudflare - Global delivery via edge networks.
ucfitness_page.arch_desc: A custom caching layer is implemented to avoid hitting API limits as user count grows. Instead of making API calls per individual user request, a server-side worker periodically collects and aggregates data, updating the database via an asynchronous aggregation architecture.

dsPrivacy.title: Dual Subtitles Privacy Policy
dsPrivacy.scope_desc: This policy covers the Google Chrome extension “Dual Subtitles” (the “extension”) published by Studio344. For the Studio344 website, see the site privacy policy. The extension uses no cookies, no Google Analytics, and no Google AdSense.
dsPrivacy.access_desc: While a Prime Video or Netflix playback page is open, the extension observes the playback information those services deliver to their own player, in order to find the subtitle tracks the title ships. From it the extension reads subtitle track lists, their languages and types, and the subtitle URLs the service itself published. It also reads the subtitle line the service draws on the page, which it needs to place its own lines and, when a chosen language has no official track, to translate. All of this is processed locally in the page and in the extension and is never sent anywhere.
dsPrivacy.transmit_desc: The extension does not send subtitle text, viewing URLs, watch history, titles watched, or settings to the developer or to any third party. It has no telemetry, analytics, advertising, account service, external translation API, or remote SDK.
dsPrivacy.transmit_license: The extension makes exactly one kind of outbound request of its own: a request to api.gumroad.com carrying the product identifier, the licence key, and a true/false flag telling Gumroad whether to count this check as an activation of that key. Nothing else.
dsPrivacy.transmit_when: It is made in two situations, both of which require a Pro licence key to have been entered. When the key is first entered and checked, at the user's request. And, for as long as a licence is stored, at most once a day, to notice a membership that has ended or whose payment has failed. That re-check is not prompted by the user: the extension's service worker keeps a timer of its own for it, and a settings popup or settings page that is opened also runs it if a day has passed. It is never started by opening a video page, so when it happens says nothing about what, or whether, anyone is watching.
dsPrivacy.transmit_contents: No subtitle text, no URL, no title, and no identifier of the user's viewing is included in either request. Users of the free tier who never enter a key generate no outbound request at all.
dsPrivacy.transmit_subtitle: Subtitle files themselves are fetched from the services' own subtitle URLs. Only an exact URL discovered in that service's own playback information may be fetched; a URL that was never discovered is refused before any network access occurs.
dsPrivacy.limited_desc: The extension uses playback and subtitle data only to provide its clearly disclosed, user-facing features: dual-subtitle display, subtitle selection, text cleanup, and on-device translation. It does not use this data for advertising, profiling, creditworthiness, or any unrelated purpose. It does not sell or transfer this data to the developer or to third parties, and it does not permit human access to it.
dsPrivacy.storage_desc: The extension stores the following six things, and nothing else.
dsPrivacy.storage_list_1: Settings (chrome.storage.sync): the two chosen subtitle languages, per-line font size and colour, whether that size follows the size of the video, placement, and the CC cleanup switches. These synchronise through the user's own Chrome profile; the developer cannot read them.
dsPrivacy.storage_list_2: Licence verification result (chrome.storage.sync): the licence key entered and the time until which its verification is trusted offline.
dsPrivacy.storage_list_3: Free-tier usage (chrome.storage.local): a per-day count of seconds during which the extension's subtitles were actually on screen. It stays on the device and records only a date and a number of seconds — no titles, no URLs, no times of day.
dsPrivacy.storage_list_4: Review-request signal (chrome.storage.local): up to three dates on which the extension drew both subtitle lines from official tracks for at least five minutes. It decides whether the settings popup asks, once, for a store review. Dates and a count of seconds only — no titles, no URLs — and it stays on the device.
dsPrivacy.storage_list_5: Review-request state (chrome.storage.local): how many times that ask has been shown and whether it should stop. This stays on the device. Whether a review was written is neither recorded nor knowable to the developer.
dsPrivacy.storage_list_6: Licence end note (chrome.storage.sync): when Gumroad reports that a stored licence is no longer valid, the reason — the membership ended, a payment failed, or it was refunded — and the time, so the plan section can say why Pro stopped. It holds no key and no payment detail, and is removed when a licence is activated again or the user closes the note.
dsPrivacy.storage_memory: Subtitle text and the subtitle cues fetched for playback are held in memory for the tab and are not written to persistent storage.
dsPrivacy.translate_desc: When a chosen language has no official subtitle track for a title, the extension translates the service's own subtitle line using Chrome's built-in Translator API. That translation runs on the device through Chrome; no subtitle text is sent to an external translation service. Chrome may download a language model for a language pair the first time it is used, which is a request made by Chrome to Google rather than by this extension.
dsPrivacy.drm_desc: The extension does not acquire, decrypt, or bypass DRM, video data, or playback entitlements, and it does not alter the services' playback requests. It reads the subtitle information those services already deliver to their own player.
dsPrivacy.perm_list_1: activeTab: read the state of the playback tab in front of the user, so the settings surfaces can report and change it.
dsPrivacy.perm_list_2: storage: store the settings, licence verification result, and free-tier usage listed above.
dsPrivacy.perm_list_3: https://api.gumroad.com/*: verify a Pro licence key when the user enters it, and re-check a stored one at most once a day. No other host is permitted.
dsPrivacy.perm_list_4: alarms: wake the service worker every few hours so a stored Pro licence is re-checked at most once a day, on a timer unrelated to viewing. When no licence key has been entered it wakes the worker and nothing else happens.
dsPrivacy.perm_scope: Content scripts run only on Prime Video, Amazon Video, and Netflix addresses. There are no broad host permissions.
dsPrivacy.payment_desc: Pro is a subscription sold and billed by Gumroad. Payment, account, and card details are entered on Gumroad's own site under Gumroad's terms and privacy practices; none of that data is entered into, handled by, or visible to the extension. The extension only ever sends Gumroad what verifying a licence key needs — when the key is entered, and for a stored key at most once a day.
dsPrivacy.children_desc: The extension is not directed at children and collects no personal information from anyone.
dsPrivacy.changes_desc: Material changes to this policy will be published on this page with an updated date, and the extension's version will be raised in the same change.
dsPrivacy.contact_desc: Questions about this policy: please use the contact page.
